title: Billing Desk Note: FloodGuard Electronic-Payment Credit
content:
Desk note for the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy — electronic-payment credit on the renewal payment.

An electronic-payment credit reduces the renewal payment by 1.5 percent of the premium charged for the new term when the named insured's own premium payments received on the policy within the last 36 months were all made by EFT or card; by 0.5 percent of that premium when the named insured's payments in that window were made both by EFT or card and by check; and by nothing when none of the named insured's payments in that window was made by EFT or card.

**What is looked at.** The premium payments received on this policy's premium account within the 36 months up to the date of the renewal payment, and only those received from the named insured; a payment made by the mortgagee is not one of the named insured's payments. For each, the method on record: EFT, card or check.

**Condition matrix**

| Named insured's payments in the 36 months include EFT or card | …include check | Electronic-payment credit |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | 1.5 percent |
| Yes | Yes | 0.5 percent |
| No | Yes | none |
| No | No (no payment from the named insured in the window) | none |

**Hypothetical cases** (illustrative inputs; premium charged for the new term 1,000.00 in each):

- Three EFT payments and one card payment in the window, no check: 1.5 percent, which is 15.00.
- Two EFT payments and one check in the window: 0.5 percent, which is 5.00.
- Only checks in the window: none.
- The only payments in the window were made by the mortgagee: none, since the named insured made no EFT or card payment in it.
- A card payment made 37 months before the renewal payment and only checks since: none, since the card payment lies outside the 36 months.
